lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
List your success criteria and how you will measure pass/fail in the test.

FEEDBACK
Measurable checks e.g. holds n items for t minutes without falling.

WATCH FOR
Declaring success without a test against criteria is incomplete.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Build, test, improve and retest your solution. Record criteria results before and after the improvement. Photo/sketch the final prototype.

Write a short reflection naming one observation or step you corrected and why.

Parent: Likely misconception: Declaring success without a test against criteria is incomplete. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Investigate or describe a fresh example (not the worked objects) that uses make. Record evidence and explain how it supports your claim.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one science misconception about make, correct it with evidence, and say why the correction works.

WORKED MODEL

teach_steps.explain:
Making and testing a solution follows the brief: build a prototype, test against criteria, improve once with evidence, retest.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on observation, fair tests and design evidence, rather than guessing from a picture alone. Keep every claim linked to what was seen or measured.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the observations, properties or test steps that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a result is uncertain, identify what would have to be observed or tested again. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
teach_steps.notice: Declaring success without a test against criteria is incomplete. Correct the claim or method, not just the neatness of the diagram.
